transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How may I help you?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Got my notes beside me, so quite convenient to talk now. Hoping to keep this call short, though. I'm trying not to spend the whole afternoon on the phone.

Of course. Before we discuss the account, please provide your identification details.

My NRIC is S zero nine zero zero eight three nine Q. My date of birth is 2 March 1993.

Thank you, Adrian. What would you like to cover today?

For this transaction, use my existing holding in Harbor SGD Bond Fund. I want to sell from my existing holding. My notes have 2,000 units as the possible sale size. Let me settle the terms before deciding.

Your objective is to free up money from your existing holding for planned personal expenditure and reduce your exposure to changes in its value. I'll keep the discussion focused and leave room for any questions you want to raise.

Thanks. These days I'm trying to spend more time with family. Work always got something waiting, but cannot keep letting that take up the whole day. Even when we're out together, my phone keeps ringing.

It sounds as though having fewer interruptions would be welcome. For routine updates, would you prefer a concise telephone conversation rather than a longer discussion?

Short call better lah. Tell me the main point, then leave space for me to ask. If too much information all together, I end up searching through my notes while the person is still talking.

I can keep that preference in mind and pause between topics. I recommend reducing your holding in Harbor SGD Bond Fund because it releases money for your planned expenditure and reduces your ongoing exposure to interest-rate and credit-related fluctuations.

But the returns, can you guarantee them or not? I prefer to know what's certain before I decide.

No, I cannot guarantee future investment returns or promise a particular financial outcome. With Harbor SGD Bond Fund, rising market interest rates can lower the value of the bonds it holds, which can reduce the fund's unit value. Do you understand how rising interest rates could reduce the value of your holding in this fund?

Yes, I understand. Rates go up, the bonds inside can drop in value, so my holding can be worth less also.

The transaction fee for this sale is 0.2% of the transaction amount. You may lose some or all of the capital you invested in this fund. Selling below what you paid would crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss on this sale in order to obtain the liquidity you need?

Yes, I'm willing to accept a loss on this sale. Need the money for my planned expenses, so I can bear that outcome. Just let me get back to the right part of my notes. I wrote some family arrangements on the same page, now everything mixed together.

Take your time. I'll pause while you find your place, and then we can finish the call.

Found it already. Do the transaction in Singapore dollars, please. The transaction amount I want is 1,000,000. Use the quantity from my notes that I mentioned earlier lah. That's the size I want for this sale. Make it a limit order, with the minimum sale price per unit set at 500 Singapore dollars. Don't execute below that, please.

Please confirm your final instruction: sell 2,000 units of Harbor SGD Bond Fund using a limit order, with a minimum price per unit of 500 Singapore dollars and a transaction amount of 1,000,000 in Singapore dollars. Do you authorise me to place that order?

Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please place the order exactly as you've just stated.

Thank you, Adrian. That concludes the instruction-taking part of our call. If we need to contact you about administration, we can keep the conversation focused on the relevant point.

That would help. Usually I can step away from work for a short call, just not sit there talking for ages. Thanks for leaving me time to check my page.

You're welcome. Thank you for calling, and enjoy your time with your family.

Thanks, Rachel. Better put the phone away now before another work call comes in. Bye.
